mentions.name: Postkit
mentions.description: This app provides a Postgres-based foundation for building applications, bundling the application-independent basics like login and permissions so developers can start a new app with it and add their own features with consistent structure.
mentions.problem: With vibe coding/LLM-assisted engineering it is hard to get the basic, application-independent stuff correct, so this provides a consistent base to build on.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Postkit: https://github.com/varunchopra/postkit

This is basically my version of "what all could you throw into Postgres?"

My problem with vibe coding/LLM assisted engineering is that it's hard to get the basic stuff that is independent of the application itself, correct, so I just use this and make sure everything I build has some consistency.

You can pop this in and use it as the base for your app and add login, permissions, etc. quite cleanly.

mentions.name: Postkit
mentions.description: Postkit provides auth, permissions, config, usage metering, and job queues as pure SQL functions inside Postgres, so new apps get backend infrastructure built in without external services. It implements Zanzibar-style ReBAC permissions, a double-entry ledger for usage metering, and transactional job queues using SKIP LOCKED, comprising about 15k lines of SQL across five modules with a Python SDK; the SQL works from any language.
mentions.problem: When quickly spinning up apps with Claude Code, the same infrastructure is needed every time - user auth, permissions, usage tracking, and job queues - requiring external services to set up and slowing iteration.
mentions.audience: Developers spinning up new apps (especially with AI coding assistants like Claude Code) who need ready-made backend infrastructure.
